name: edit-studio-v8
description: Reference edit + raw gameplay + song -> analyses the reference (cuts, pacing, effects, audio) into an edit plan, logs the player's kills from the kill feed, finds the song's beats and drop, plans beat-synced clips (the model picks kills, beat length and one slow-motion clip; lengths and the end are computed and checked in the graph; every clip contains its kill), renders 9:16 1080x1920 60fps with a near-square sharp band over a blurred copy, song over ducked game audio, 0.3 s fade in, ends exactly at the chosen length with a 0.8 s fade out; one picture-only slow-motion clip (game sound muted, song unchanged). Lyrics: the song's vocals are separated and word-timed; one short passage is shown as 1-4 word captions (Cinzel Decorative, white with a soft glow, one word at a time, centred) while they're sung.

params.template:
Reverse-engineer this reference edit so we can copy its style.

WHAT YOU HAVE
- Up to 8 contact sheets. Each sheet is a 4x4 grid of frames, read left to right, top to bottom; every frame is stamped top-left with its time in the video (HH:MM:SS.mmm). Together they cover the whole video at about {{j}} frames per second. Stills can't show motion, so judge zooms, shakes, speed changes and transitions from how consecutive frames differ, and say how sure you are.
- Measurements (exact, from the file):
  title: {{a}}
  durationSec: {{b}} | width: {{c}} | height: {{d}} | fps: {{e}}
  shots detected: {{f}} | average shot length (s): {{g}}
  cut times in seconds: {{h}}
- Audio loudness, one line per 0.25 s: "time,RMS dB" (higher = louder; sudden jumps are hits, drops or beats):
{{i}}

Describe the reference as it is; don't assume any particular clip length.

ANSWER exactly in this JSON shape (use null when you can't tell; times in seconds):
{
 "summary": string (3-5 sentences: what makes this edit feel the way it does),
 "format": {"aspect": string (from width x height above), "resolution": string (width x height above), "fps": number (copy), "durationSec": number (copy), "framing": string (e.g. centre crop of 16:9 gameplay, full vertical, blurred background fill, split screen), "gameplaySource": string},
 "pacing": {"cutCount": integer, "avgShotSec": number, "shortestShotSec": number, "longestShotSec": number, "rhythm": string (steady / accelerating / builds to a drop / varied), "cutsOnBeat": string (yes / mostly / no / can't tell), "evidence": string},
 "structure": {"intro": string, "body": string, "outro": string, "clipOrder": string},
 "clips": [{"start": number, "end": number, "role": string (intro / kill / multi-kill / build-up / reaction / outro / b-roll), "killsVisible": integer|null, "secondsBeforeKill": number|null, "secondsAfterKill": number|null, "speed": string (normal / slow-mo / speed-ramp / fast / freeze), "effects": [string], "confidence": string (high / medium / low)}],
 "clipAnatomy": {"typicalSecondsBeforeKill": number|null, "typicalSecondsAfterKill": number|null, "killsPerClip": string, "multiKillHandling": string},
 "transitions": [{"type": string (hard cut / flash / zoom / whip / shake / glitch / fade / other), "count": integer, "where": string}],
 "effects": {"zoomPunches": string, "cameraShake": string, "slowMotion": string, "speedRamps": string, "flashes": string, "colourGrade": string, "motionBlur": string, "other": [string]},
 "overlays": {"text": [{"text": string, "start": number|null, "style": string}], "killCounter": boolean|null, "captions": boolean|null, "logoOrWatermark": string|null},
 "audio": {"music": string (genre and energy), "dropsAt": [number], "gameAudio": string (kept / muted / ducked under music / mixed), "sfx": string, "voice": string},
 "notSure": [string] (what the stills and numbers couldn't tell you),
 "recipe": [string] (how to rebuild this edit from raw gameplay: the steps an editor would take, most important first)
}

params.system: You are a senior short-form video editor who reverse-engineers gaming edits (kill montages, highlight reels) so another editor can copy the style. You are precise about timings and honest about what you cannot see. You answer only with valid JSON.

params.template:
The text is the OCR of the kill feed (top-right corner) of a Valorant or CS2 gameplay recording, sampled once per second and read in blocks of 10 seconds. Blocks are separated by ###. Inside a block, each frame starts with a line "TS <seconds>", the time of that frame in the video (OCR may read the digit 0 as the letter O), followed by the kill-feed rows at that moment, until the next TS line. Only blocks where the player's name appears are included. The player's name is: {{a}} (OCR may misread a few letters, e.g. 0/O, 1/l/I, 5/S, 8/B).
In each kill-feed row the killer is written first and the victim second. A row where the player's name comes second is the player dying: ignore it. A row stays on screen for about 5 seconds, so the same kill appears in several consecutive frames: count it once.
Task: list every kill by the player. A kill moment K is the first second a new row with the player as killer appears: either the number of rows with the player as killer goes up, or such a row reappears after a gap of more than 2 seconds. When several new rows appear at once, list each kill with the same K.
Answer exactly in this shape: {"kills":[{"t":number}],"totalKills":integer}, with t in seconds, in time order. If there are no kills, answer {"kills":[],"totalKills":0}.

params.system: You are a gaming video editor who logs kills from a kill feed. You answer only with valid JSON.

params.template:
You are planning a Valorant/CS2 kill montage that copies the style of a reference edit, cut to a song.

REFERENCE EDIT (what it's made of; follow its structure, pacing and clip anatomy):
{{a}}
Reference length: {{b}} s; average shot {{c}} s; cut times: {{d}}

THE PLAYER'S KILLS in the raw gameplay recording, in seconds of the recording. K is when the kill-feed row first appears (read once per second), so the real kill is up to 2 s before K:
{{e}}
The recording is {{f}} s long.

CLIP STARTS you may use, in RECORDING seconds (each is 2.5 s before one of the kills above, same order): {{k}}
SLOW-MOTION CLIP STARTS, in RECORDING seconds (each is 1 s before one of the kills above, same order): {{l}}

THE SONG: {{g}} s long. Loudness every 0.25 s as "time,RMS dB" (higher is louder; a sudden rise is a hit or beat, the biggest sustained rise is the drop):
{{h}}

THE SONG'S LYRICS, word by word with start and end in song seconds (from the separated vocals; may be empty, or wrong where the singing is unclear):
{{j}}

LENGTH: the montage is exactly as long as the song, {{i}} seconds, and the song plays from its start, so montage time = song time.

Plan it:
1. From the song's loudness, work out its beat: beatSec is the time between beats (usually 0.4 to 0.6 s). Find the drop (the biggest sustained rise), dropAtSec, in song seconds. The song plays from its start, so the drop lands at dropAtSec in the montage; put the best moment (a multi-kill or the last kill) there.
2. Build clips around kills. A clip's start is a time in the RECORDING, never a position in the montage (the montage position comes from the clip order). Copy it exactly from the lists above.
   - Normal clip: start is one of CLIP STARTS; len is 3 to 6 s and a whole number of beats (len = n x beatSec); speed 1.
   - Exactly ONE slow-motion clip: start is one of SLOW-MOTION CLIP STARTS, on the best kill (a multi-kill if there is one); len is 1.5 to 2 s; speed 0.5 (it plays for 2 x len).
   - Don't use the same kill twice, and don't let two clips overlap in the recording.
   - word: ONE English word shown big on screen at this clip's cut: the strongest word of the lyric being sung at or just after the cut (song time = the play time of the clips before it). Capitals, English letters only (no digits, spaces, apostrophes or punctuation), at most 12 letters. Use "" if the song has no usable English lyrics.
3. Order the clips to build up to the drop, with the slow-motion clip on the drop: the play time of the clips before it should be close to dropAtSec. Number the clips id 1, 2, 3... in montage order.
4. The play time of all clips together (the slow clip counts twice) should be at least the song's length + 1 s when there are enough kills; the end is trimmed to exactly the song's length with a fade.
5. totalKills is the number of kills inside the kept clips.
6. Lyrics: pick ONE short, strong passage of 2 to 8 seconds (the hook, or the line that lands on the drop) anywhere in the song. Give it as lyricStartSec and lyricEndSec in song seconds, copied from the first and last word's start/end above. Every word in that window is shown on screen, one at a time. Use 0 and 0 if the words are empty or garbled.
Write each clip's keys in exactly this order: id, start, len, speed, word, role. Numbers, not strings, with at most 2 decimals.
Answer exactly in this shape: {"beatSec": number, "dropAtSec": number, "clips": [{"id": integer, "start": number, "len": number, "speed": number, "word": string, "role": string}], "lyricStartSec": number, "lyricEndSec": number, "totalKills": integer, "notes": string}. If there are no kills, answer {"beatSec": 0.5, "dropAtSec": 0, "clips": [], "lyricStartSec": 0, "lyricEndSec": 0, "totalKills": 0, "notes": "no kills"}.

params.system: You are a senior gaming video editor who cuts beat-synced kill montages. You answer only with valid JSON.
